summary: Crow's nest in a topped tree above Mosetown, Douglas County, built 1942 and listed as gone; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Crow's nest in a tree topped at 96 feet, with an 8x8 foot platform reached by a salvaged steel ladder
facts.status_note: No source we read describes what remains at the site.

resolved_conflicts.field: height and date of the crow's nest
resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com gives a 92-foot crow's nest from the 1930s and a cabin in 1943. The 1942 Forest Log reports, as quoted on Forest Lookouts, give a tree topped at 96 feet, built in August 1942, and a split board structure in 1943. The story follows the 1942 reports because they were written at the time; the record height of 29.3 m matches 96 feet.

resolved_conflicts.field: name of the fire association and the warden's initials
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The May 1942 report calls the body the Western Lane County Fire Patrol association and names Ray Oglesby as warden; the August 1942 report names H.R. Oglesby and the Western Lane Forest Protective Association. The story uses the August name and gives only the warden's surname.

notes_for_editor: Two WebSearch calls found nothing on this lookout beyond the three pages above. The 1942 Forest Log items are reprinted only on the Forest Lookouts page and are cited through it. The story names Oglesby and J.W. 'Pete' Kibby, both from the 1942 reports, and gives no other staffing names. No source describes the site today or says whether it is public, so access is not recorded. The brief's status gone is supported by the firelookout.org index. The height of 29.3 m is a conversion of the 96-foot tree top; firelookout.com gives 92 feet. Verification 2026-10-10: the story's 'newspaper' label was changed to Forest Log, and evidence quotes were added for the 90-foot ladder, the April 25 start, the two boats, the Kibby name and the Douglas County listing.
